indian.headline: Indian markets closed slightly lower on weak banking and mixed sector cues, but FPI inflows and rupee strength offer support.
indian.lead: Indian markets closed slightly lower on weak banking and mixed sector cues, but FPI inflows and rupee strength offer support.
indian.brief: Sensex fell 0.22%, Nifty 50 dropped 0.14%, and Bank Nifty slid 0.41% as banking stocks underperformed, though IT gained 0.2%.
indian.narrative:
Indian equities ended a down day on 24 August, with all three headline indices in the red. The Sensex lost 0.22%, Nifty 50 fell 0.14%, and Bank Nifty declined 0.41%, reflecting broader caution in financial stocks. However, the day had bright spots: the rupee strengthened to 95.64 per dollar on RBI support and strong capital inflows, while IT stocks rose 0.2%, bucking the trend. Banking and pharma sectors dragged the market down with losses of 0.4% and 0.1% respectively.

Underlying sentiment remained mixed. Foreign portfolio investors returned aggressively, deploying ₹43,744 crore in July–August after months of heavy selling, signalling renewed confidence in India's earnings and IPO market. However, regulatory warnings about retail derivatives trading cast a shadow: SEBI found that 90% of Indian retail F&O traders lose money, and 89% of traders under 30 suffered losses in FY26. On the corporate front, Vishal Mega Mart hit the upper circuit after reappointing its founder as MD, while IPO activity remained mixed, with Horizon Industrial Parks listing flat and Hy-Tech Engineers drawing strong grey market demand.
